sentences.text:

2. Heard Ms.P.Harshini, learned counsel representing Mr.Satheesh Kumar Eerla, learned counsel for petitioner, Mr.Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent No.1-State.

3. The petitioner is accused No.1 in C.C.No.2381 of 2024 facing accusation under Sections 420, 447,
427, 294-B and 506 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that though the petitioner got a strong case even for quashment, as he is determined to see the process through, the insistence for his presence is causing severe difficulty in pursuing his avocation.
Therefore, prayed for dispensing his personal appearance in the proceedings, unless presence in person is required and such direction would redress his grievance.

5. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor submits that there is no specific objection for the prayer,
however pleaded for a direction for appearance of the petitioner on the material stages in the proceedings.
6.

Having regard to the submissions, subject to the petitioner's appearance through his counsel on every adjournment and the petitioner's presence as and when directed by the Court, the in-person presence of the petitioner in the proceedings of the C.C.No.2381 of 2024 on the file of I Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate at Hanamkonda, is dispensed with.
